title: Distance between feature vectors
goals: Explain how units and chosen features affect similarity

prerequisite.prompt: What does abs(3 - 7) measure? If unfamiliar, calculate the positive gap.

vocabulary: An ordered list of numeric features
A number describing difference under a chosen rule
The sum of absolute feature differences
Rescaling features to a comparable scale

blocks.text: A fictional activity chooser represents each activity with energy and group-work ratings on a 0 to 5 scale. A learner requests [2, 4]. We compare options by adding absolute differences. This is a chosen rule for similarity; it is not a learned model or an objective measure of quality.

blocks.title: Python 3 code
blocks.text:
target = [2, 4]
options = {"Sketch": [1, 3], "Relay": [5, 4]}
for name in options:
    features = options[name]
    distance = (abs(features[0] - target[0])
                + abs(features[1] - target[1]))
    print(name, distance)

blocks.title: Follow the evidence
blocks.caption: Read each row from left to right and connect the evidence to the stated rule.

blocks.text: abs gives a nonnegative gap. Under this rule Sketch is closer. Feature order must match: first energy, then group work. Both scales are 0 to 5, but that does not prove one unit has identical practical meaning in both features.

blocks.label: Find the distance from target [2, 4] to [2, 4] and to [3, 3].

blocks.text: If one feature is duration in minutes up to 60 and another a rating up to 5, raw distance may be dominated by duration. Specify scaling or weights before ranking; do not silently change units to get a preferred winner.

Similarity depends on the features collected and the distance rule. Missing accessibility, cost or preference information can make the closest item unsuitable. Hard requirements should be checked separately.

blocks.label: Two activities have distance zero. Must they suit every learner equally well?

workbook.title: Read a vector
workbook.prompt: For [4, 1] under the worked feature order, identify energy and group-work ratings.

workbook.title: Compute distances
workbook.prompt: From target [1, 2], find distances to A [2, 2] and B [0, 4].

workbook.title: Repair feature order
workbook.prompt: One record uses [group work, energy] while others use [energy, group work]. Why is the distance unreliable?
workbook.answer: It compares different meanings in each position. Reorder using the documented schema before computing.

workbook.title: Rank independently
workbook.prompt: Target is [3, 2]. Options A [1, 2], B [3, 4], C [4, 2]. Calculate distances, select the closest, and identify a tie among the others.
workbook.answer: Distances A 2, B 2, C 1. C is closest; A and B tie. Do not claim a unique ranking of the tied pair without a rule.

workbook.title: Limit similarity
workbook.prompt: Two activities have distance zero. Must they suit every learner equally well?
workbook.answer: No. Only the recorded features match; unrecorded needs and activity details may differ.

teacher.background: Teach Week 22 as a two-session investigation using fictional data. A fictional activity chooser represents each activity with energy and group-work ratings on a 0 to 5 scale. A learner requests [2, 4]. We compare options by adding absolute differences. This is a chosen rule for similarity; it is not a learned model or an objective measure of quality. Assess the three stated outcomes through the independent task, not by copying the worked result.

Paper trace table and the student workbook

sessions: Retrieve the prerequisite and explain the purpose in the opening section.

Complete W1 and W2, then compare predictions with observed results.
Collect the guided prediction before running; discuss a mismatch and its cause.
Retrieve the main rule without showing the previous answer.
Use W3 to diagnose and repair the stated failure; rerun an earlier case.
Collect W4 independently, including code or plan, predictions and explanations, before hints.
Discuss W5 and the exit; use the fresh retry when support was needed.
teacher.guidedAnswer: Distances 0 and 2. Zero means identical recorded features, not identical activities in every way. Exit: No. Only the recorded features match; unrecorded needs and activity details may differ.
